note: DNS label attributes are routed into the DNS-label decoder using attacker-controlled packet bytes.
The decoder interprets the current byte as a compressed pointer when the input-controlled label byte is above 63.
A pointer must refer to an earlier label position; this safety obligation prevents loops and invalid backward traversal.
The code dereferences the pointer target byte to validate it, which is the invalid read site when the crafted pointer lands on an unsafe location.
